cards.name: Hardware-aware model autoselection
cards.nugget: Estimate per-host tok/s by blending GPU VRAM bandwidth and system-RAM bandwidth weighted by the offload fraction, then pick the largest model that clears a target throughput — calibrated against real measurements, not spec sheets.
cards.why_now: G1's which-model-on-which-host table is hand-maintained; this is the exact automation it's missing.
cards.first_step: Benchmark 2-3 models per host to calibrate the bandwidth→tok/s estimator, then compare predictions to the current manual table.
cards.notes: Bullseye for G1. Build in-stack: it's a small estimator, not a framework. Calibration honesty is the whole value — don't trust the model without per-host measurement.

cards.name: Grammar-constrained decoding for local LLMs
cards.nugget: Constrain the sampler to a formal grammar (GBNF / JSON-schema-derived) so malformed output is structurally impossible — eliminates the parse-retry loop entirely rather than mitigating it.
cards.why_now: G4 is the single most direct hit; grammar constraint is the strongest known fix for small-model structured output.
cards.first_step: Convert the target JSON schema to GBNF and pass it to the existing llama.cpp server's grammar param on one structured endpoint; measure parse-failure rate before/after.
cards.notes: Buy: GBNF ships in llama.cpp and outlines is maintained — reimplementing a grammar-constrained sampler is a major project with no upside. Pairs with c15 for fields a grammar can't fully constrain (semantics).

cards.name: Capability-scoped tool tokens
cards.nugget: Issue short-lived tokens that grant only named capabilities (email.read, memory.write) and gate every tool/DB access behind a capability check, with an explicit no-bypass doctrine — least-privilege for agents.
cards.why_now: G3 is wholly unbuilt — every agent has unscoped DB access today; this is the only candidate that addresses it.
cards.first_step: Define a capability enum and route one agent's DB access through a token-checked wrapper before generalizing.
cards.notes: Build: it's a thin in-stack layer, not a dependency. Doubles as strong G6 portfolio material (safety rails for autonomous agents).

cards.name: Litestream streaming replication for SQLite
cards.nugget: Stream SQLite WAL frames to a replica/object store for point-in-time recovery and a single-writer replication story without changing the DB engine.
cards.notes: Real, well-maintained technique, but G2 is now substantially handled by the cockpit-reconcile engine — downrank per the open-problems note. If ever adopted, buy Litestream; never clone WAL shipping.

cards.name: LLM-as-judge eval harness with pairwise rubric
cards.nugget: Rubric-driven LLM judging plus pairwise comparison and decoy/holdout controls to catch grader gaming — an offline eval loop with built-in anti-gaming validity checks.
cards.why_now: G6 wants demonstrable eval loops; anton-scout already runs decoy-injection eval, so this is directly on-mission and extends existing work.
cards.first_step: Add a pairwise mode to the existing decoy eval so two candidate outputs are judged head-to-head against the rubric, not just scored absolutely.
cards.notes: Build: the harness already exists in-repo; this is an incremental extension, not a new dependency. Decoy/holdout control is the part that gives the eval credibility.

cards.name: AutoSwarm AGI Operating System
cards.notes: Pure VC narrative — 'thousands of AGI agents replace your team', waitlist. No transferable technique; fabricating one would be the worst outcome.

cards.name: On-chain RAG with blockchain prompt provenance
cards.notes: Web3 buzzword soup. Blockchain/NFT provenance adds nothing to retrieval for a solo, local-first operator; a local hash log would do any real job here.

cards.name: Disaggregated prefill/decode inference serving
cards.nugget: Split prefill and decode onto separate GPU pools and transfer KV-cache between them to maximize throughput.
cards.notes: Genuinely real datacenter technique, but scale-only (10k+ QPS, RDMA, multi-tenant) — wrong context for a solo fleet. Maps to no listed gap.

cards.name: Multi-region Kubernetes autoscaling for LLM gateways
cards.nugget: Autoscale gateway pods across regions with global load balancing and spot bin-packing.
cards.notes: Scale-only and an anti-goal (new always-on cluster machinery). No relevance to one operator on a local fleet.

cards.name: MetaCognition prompt-chaining
cards.nugget: A plan→act→reflect→revise loop over a scratchpad — a structured self-correction pass layered on single calls.
cards.notes: The reflect loop is a real (well-worn) pattern; the 'metacognition/self-awareness' framing is hype. Extra calls per task tension with G8 — skip unless a specific task needs the self-correction.

cards.name: Mixture-of-Agents ensembling
cards.nugget: Layered ensemble where each layer sees prior layers' outputs, aggregating multiple models for quality.
cards.notes: Real but runs many calls/query — directly opposes G8 token budgeting. Wrong economics for solo local-first.

cards.name: Speculative decoding with a small draft model
cards.nugget: A small draft model proposes several tokens that the full model verifies in one forward pass — lower latency, bit-identical output.
cards.why_now: Free latency win that helps small models meet timeouts under load (the latency half of G4).
cards.first_step: Enable speculative decoding in llama.cpp/vLLM with a small draft model on one host and measure tok/s.
cards.notes: Buy: built into llama.cpp/vLLM. Cuts latency, not token cost or schema-adherence — so it eases G4 timeouts but isn't a structured-output fix.

cards.name: Prompt caching for reused system blocks
cards.nugget: Mark the stable system/preamble block as cacheable so repeated runs reuse it instead of re-paying first-token cost — KV reuse locally, native prompt cache on metered APIs.
cards.why_now: Usage instrumentation just landed with no baseline — this is the cheapest, highest-leverage token cut to measure first.
cards.first_step: Mark the stable system preamble cacheable on the T3 Claude path and enable KV reuse for the reused local preamble.
cards.notes: Buy on the Claude side (native prompt caching); trivially build local KV reuse. Small local nodes 're-sending state' (per G8) is exactly what this kills.

cards.name: Transactional outbox on SQLite
cards.nugget: Record side-effects in an outbox table inside the same transaction as the state change, then have a single writer drain it — exactly-once local job processing and single-writer discipline without a message broker.
cards.why_now: The single-writer-drains pattern complements the cockpit-reconcile engine and removes the need for any new broker daemon.
cards.first_step: Add an outbox table for one side-effecting job and route all writes through a single drainer process.
cards.notes: Maps G2 but that gap is downranked post-reconcile, so scored modestly. Unlike c4 this is the single-writer *discipline* G2 actually wants (not replication), and it's broker-free — fits the anti-goals. Build in-stack.

cards.name: Schema-validated repair for small-model JSON
cards.nugget: On schema-validation failure, feed the exact validator error back for one bounded repair pass instead of a blind retry — cheap, targeted structured-output reliability.
cards.why_now: Direct G4 hit and near-trivial to add; catches the semantic/field errors a grammar (c2) can't, at the cost of at most one extra call.
cards.first_step: Wrap the structured-output call: validate against the schema, and on failure issue one repair prompt containing the validator's error message; cap at a single repair.
cards.notes: Build: ~30 lines around an existing validator. Best paired with c2 (grammar guarantees parse; repair fixes semantics). Bound the repair to one pass so it never becomes an unbounded retry loop (also a G8 concern).

cards.name: Embedding-based contradiction surfacing
cards.nugget: Embed a personal corpus locally and use cosine similarity to surface passages that negate a given claim, ranked by a confidence score — a contradiction layer over notes.
cards.why_now: A tidy local-retrieval demo with real personal utility, and good portfolio signal for retrieval.
cards.first_step: Embed notes locally and prototype ranking cosine-near passages that contradict a test claim.
cards.notes: Real but niche. Naive cosine alone surfaces 'related', not strictly 'contradicting' — needs an NLI/judge step to be honest. Retrieval portfolio value (G6), possible creative-corpus use (G7).

cards.name: KV-cache quantization for longer local context
cards.nugget: Quantize the KV cache (e.g. 4-bit) so a model holds longer context in the same VRAM, trading a little quality for headroom on a single consumer GPU.
cards.why_now: More usable context on existing consumer GPUs without buying hardware — relieves the context-pressure side of G8/G1.
cards.first_step: Enable 4-bit KV-cache quant in llama.cpp on the longest-context node and measure the quality delta.
cards.notes: Buy: it's a built-in flag. It's VRAM headroom, not token-count reduction — adjacent to G8's context goal and to G1 fit, not a direct cost cut.

cards.name: SentientOS self-aware agent kernel
cards.notes: Consciousness/AGI hype with a waitlist. No technique to extract.

cards.name: Decentralized trustless model marketplace
cards.notes: Web3 NFT marketplace narrative — irrelevant to a local-first operator. Nothing transferable.

cards.name: FounderBot autonomous startup-in-a-box
cards.notes: 'Replace your engineering team' Series-A hype + waitlist. No nugget.

cards.name: PromptDAO on-chain prompt registry
cards.notes: Tokenized on-chain prompt royalties — web3 hype. A local prompt registry needs no blockchain; no transferable idea here.

cards.name: MetaMind recursive metacognition engine
cards.notes: Same plan-reflect loop as c10 but wrapped in 'artificial consciousness' marketing — a repackaging of an already-extracted nugget, adding nothing new. The real technique is already captured at c10; this candidate itself is hollow.

cards.name: Multi-region vector index sharding
cards.nugget: Shard a billion-vector index across regions with global query routing and replication.
cards.notes: Scale-only (billion-vector, multi-region). A solo corpus fits in a single local index; no relevance.

cards.name: Kubernetes operator for GPU node autoscaling
cards.nugget: Autoscale GPU node pools and bin-pack inference across a cluster with spot reclaim.
cards.notes: Enterprise-cluster, scale-only, and an anti-goal (new always-on operator/daemon). Wrong context.

cards.name: RDMA KV-cache transfer across inference nodes
cards.nugget: Move KV-cache between prefill/decode servers over RDMA to sustain datacenter throughput.
cards.notes: Datacenter-scale (RDMA, multi-tenant). No consumer-fleet relevance; maps to no gap.

cards.name: Enterprise rate limiting at 10k QPS
cards.nugget: Distributed token-bucket limiter with global quota coordination across regions.
cards.notes: The token-bucket idea is trivially known and a single-process local version would be ~20 lines — but the distributed/multi-region/10k-QPS framing is irrelevant. G8 wants budget-aware *routing*, not a high-QPS limiter. Skip.

cards.name: Per-query model ensembling for benchmark gains
cards.nugget: Run an ensemble of large models per query and aggregate to squeeze benchmark points.
cards.notes: Leaderboard-maximization (near-dup of c11) at many calls per query — directly opposed to G8's cost-cutting goal. For a cost-exposed solo operator this is the wrong direction entirely. Skip.
